items.note: S1.1.1 and its infer steps give the eight-row schedule (cancel old scratch, central and side paths, restore), the net change (JV+RG)x, the central coefficients |S cap T| mod 2 and (|S cap T|-1)/2, and the three-stage signed exchange (x,y)->(-y,x) with every auxiliary value restored, exactly as in the proof at 741-765. It never gives h=100, the neighbour rules, or the wire counts W_b, W_c (767-783), so the concrete instance is left implicit.

The plan states that a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate, so the network implements D_out S D_in^{-1} and route w applies eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} on all roles. It derives this from the invariant 'stored = D_v applied to logical', as the paper does at 804-825.

Every element of the budget is stated correctly: nondegenerate labels nested on edges, <t_S,t_T>=|S cap T|-1 so neighbours are orthogonal, the only loss is h on central edges 3->4, L=Ich, the sum Wm-2N+2L, and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539. The derivation leaves out the actual label assignment (A tensor F, B tensor F, ... at times 0-7, eq. motif-labels at 975-988) and the per-edge residual table (1022-1043), so the key claim at 1061 is quoted rather than shown. The lemma's orthonormal-basis clause for binary labels (1008-1009, 1073-1102) is assumed in S2.1.2 but never stated or derived.

The rank sum s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m is stated and derived correctly: rank equals dimension change except the N source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one (1156-1167). The endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m is only named as 'the endpoint condition' in S1.1.6.3. The plan never assigns P_U to gates and sinks, and never checks P_{U_a^perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m or the zero-source/identity-sink roles (1169-1171).

The plan gives the phase frames C_U, Hamming-weight additivity mod 4 on orthogonal vectors, and one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector, which is the start of the paper's proof (1232-1257). It never states s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m, or that after the Z_{a,k} and i^{27k} corrections every role, scratch roles included, receives C^{tensor m} (1287-1314). Those endpoint corrections are not derived.

For the bit network the chain L/N<1/2, deficit N-2L_b>0, eta_b=339/22587335000000>20*2^-50, m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-20*2^-50)>m(1-eta), and so s/W<m^tau follows the paper (1319-1344); log m<20 is used only implicitly. The complex half (s_c<W_c m, eta_c=73/19906842167500, s_c/W_c<m^sigma) is never stated or derived, even though S2.3 relies on s/W<=m^sigma.

The plan uses the primitives (controlled shifts and rational units for triangular maps, a single-digit operation, cyclic row splitting) and lists tape-stream-operations and controlled-shift as dependencies. It never states the lemmas' content, such as O(V) digit permutations and moves, splits and merges, or the b^{O(1)} offset condition for controlled shifts.

The factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 (topmost row, rightmost pivot, lower-triangular operations), the O(V) triangular transforms, the conjugation order, and the three-update interchange giving a interchanges all match 1375-1447. The statement omits that q is a fixed odd prime avoiding the denominators of the fixed finite table of factors (1396-1397, 1413-1423).

Every step of the paper's proof is there: k=0 base case, cyclic split into W role streams of volume V/W, Phi_M frames giving Phi_{I_m}, the three-update interchange, exactly s recursive calls, the recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), the geometric sum, F_k=O(e^tau), and the fixed-tape parking schedule at O(V) per node. The row-divisibility hypothesis is given in S1's motivation.

The plan has the top rho=O(log e) digits made into a row field of at least W^k rows, the base-m split of the remaining width with cost O(V) sum a_j m^{j tau}=O(Ve^tau), and the padding of [2^u] to [q^e] with e=O(u). This matches 1649-1734. It leaves out the zero-row padding to a multiple of W^k (1684-1690); see the minor error recorded for S1.

The plan gives the basic identities H_0=bSCS, C^2=X, C^{-1}=-iZCZ, one kernel per residual vector, conjugation of the residual basis into slot positions by F_2 row additions, inverse children via (C^{-1})^{tensor f}=(-i)^f Z C Z, exactly s_c children on e/m axes, and H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D. This follows 1835-1940.

The plan follows the paper's proof (2013-2207): the eight conditional additions composing to (00 10)(01 11), guards and the bad set, delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^-K}, T_0 S_0^{-1} permuting only B, at most sixteen swaps and eight rotations, and repair by extract and radix sort. The S2.2 headline 'terms that vanish when K/log p->inf' is loose, but S2.2.8 states the exact bound and its conditions.

The plan has the node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)) with s calls, the q_0 row-index chunks giving at least W^{k_0} rows, child volume V/W, the recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves O(e), the internal and leaf sums, and the base-m pieces giving O(d^{lambda'}). These match 2286-2445.

S2 states the O(Vd^{lambda'}) layer that is exact until one truncation, S2.4 the guard width Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1})=o(p) from A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E and the depth-to-bits induction, and S2.5 the disk and sqrt2 2^-p error. This matches 2479-2586 and the proof at 2686-2757.

The plan gives character cancellation by the halving shift and no two-torsion, the DIF recursion leaving B_t F_t^-, the reverse procedure giving F_t^+ B_t^{-1} via H_0^2=I/2, grouping of a round into H then J_E, and the cost pieces O(TpdK), O(Tp pK^{tau-1}), O(Tp ell d^{lambda'}) with error sqrt2 ell 2^-p. These all match 2819-3200.

The plan has evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, the four products with the established multiplier, the separation |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2, centered extraction with carry in {0,1}, negacyclic wrap, shift by p+ell, and cost O(rp log(rp)). This follows 3233-3367.

The plan gives the retained LB order, the normalization identities F^-(f*g)=M(F^-f)(F^-g) and F^+F^-=I/M, the commutation P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), the error chain 3delta+eta scaled by M, and the cost. This is the proof at 3414-3494.

The identity P_s F_s=2^{2 alpha^2} B_0 P_t F_t A, the HvdH facts, B_0=D'J'C, the no-sort remark, tensoring, and the line cost O(dTp^{3/2+delta} alpha) follow 3576-3870. The statement never defines P_s, P_t as the coordinate permutations u_{tj}, v_{-sk}, and it omits the axis exposure cost O(Tpd^2(1+ell^tau)) of the tensor lemma (3824-3829, 3875-3889).

Both identities and their proofs match 3938-3987: the coefficient check for the chirp formula, F^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F^+ so RF^+R=F^+, and the normalized convolution rule giving (u*v)/S^2. The chirp a_j=exp(-pi i sum s_i j_i^2/t_i) is never written out, and getting RF_s^+ by conjugation is not stated.

The exponents, layer inequalities, sizes, alpha and gamma, the prime-interval count, disjoint intervals, S/T>1/2 by Bernoulli, alpha^4 theta_i>p, the n^{o(1)} search, and the no-wraparound bound 2q-2<T/2<S all match 4007-4193.

The plan has the isomorphism argument (image of x has order S), the triangular coordinate formula b_i=a_i+mu_i sum a_j P_j, the descending update order, the padded-box bijection, the prefix-controlled cyclic shifts, and the cost O(Tpd^2(1+ell^tau)). This matches 4204-4292.

The plan has the well-definedness (zeta y)^r=1, the diagonal isometric isomorphism, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T, and twist approximations with error 2*2^-p. This follows 4303-4402.

The plan gives the source transform (A, chirp transform, B_0, scale 2^gamma) with exact counterpart RF_s, the six-step algorithm, and the role of the two scales by S, (u*v)/S^2 -> (u*v)/S -> 2^{2b+4}(u*v), matching 4456-4544. The input digit scaling by 2^{-b-2} is left implicit.

The plan chains errors through contractions with disk margins (.701 ring margin, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, (3E_s+2) after the opposite transform), down to the final bound 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2 using S<=T<2^b, L<b and gamma<=b/4, then rounding and carries. This follows 4557-4806, although the intermediate E_ring<5TL and chirp 8TL bounds are not listed.

All seven table rows and margins g_1..g_7, min g_i=2^-181=2kappa, the o(V) setup, absorption of log factors, and the schoolbook cutoff match 4815-4995. The reason S7.10 gives for the exceptional sorting is misattributed; see errors.
S0 says only that the bound refutes the n log n optimality conjecture in this model. It does not spell out the eventual lower bound, its liminf negation, or that the power saving gives limit zero.

errors.says: The row field divisible by W^k needed by the power-width recursion is supplied for general arrays by the chunk's own high digits.
errors.paper: The high digits give a row field of range R=q^{2 rho}>=W^k, which is generally not divisible by W^k. Zero rows are then appended within each prefix until the count is R'=W^k ceil(R/W^k)<2R, and only this padding supplies divisibility (1677-1690).

errors.says: The procedure takes O(V(L^tau+1)) time plus terms that vanish when K/log p -> infinity.
errors.paper: The extra terms M A^3 + delta_bad M A (R+A) are not small on their own. They become o(V) only when A=O(p), R exceeds every fixed polynomial in p, f<=d<=p and K/log p -> infinity (2001-2010, 2203-2207).

errors.says: Setup at recursion nodes, descriptors, prime search and the compact sorting of exceptional records are o(V) because the number of visits is polynomial in p while r exceeds every fixed power of p.
errors.paper: The superpolynomial growth of r covers per-record descriptor and setup work. The exceptional sorting is o(V) for a different reason: the bad fraction is O(d 2^-K) and K=Theta(p^{epsilon c}), so the total is O(V p^{A'} 2^-K)=o(V). Prime search is n^{o(1)} by its own estimate (4951-4973, 4160-4171).

chain: The tree reaches O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) by the paper's route: interchange, simultaneous layer, synthetic transform, ring convolution, resampling and chirp, CRT layout, then exact recovery and time accounting, each with its key quantities. It thins at the finite-network interfaces. The label assignment and residual table are quoted rather than shown. The bit endpoint identity M_sink-M_source=I_m, with the -P_{U_a} and P_{U_a^perp} terminals that achieve it, is only named. The complex interface never states s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m, its endpoint corrections to C^{tensor m}, or eta_c, yet S2.3 relies on s/W<=m^sigma.

steps.note: The plan carries the fixed network itself: the eight-row schedule on triples of [h], the net change y<-y+x for arbitrary scratch, and three stages giving (x,y)->(-y,x) with every auxiliary wire restored. It never gives h=100, the indexing of X_a, Y_a by a in T^3, N=binom(h,3)^3 or m=h^3, although N and m are used later. The verdict rests on the exchange mechanism being fully present.

S1.1.2 states that a common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, that the network implements D_out S D_in^{-1}, and that route w applies only the endpoint operator, so each edge pays only for a change of frame. This matches 804-825.

The plan has labels that are nondegenerate subspaces of an m-dimensional bilinear space built from tensor products of triple indicators, nested on every edge. The only decreasing edges are central 3->4, each losing h (S1.1.3.3, quoting 1061).

S1.1.4.4 states that matrix rank equals the dimension change on every edge except the N negative source projections, whose first edge matrix 2P_{U_a} has rank one with zero dimension change (1162-1165). The rank formula for P_V-P_U and the assignment of P_U to gates are only implicit.
The plan has the telescoping signed sum Wm-2N, L=Ich, the absolute sum Wm-2N+2L, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
The plan gives L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2, and so the deficit N-2L_b>0 and s_b<W_b m (1167).

S1.1.6.3 says that 'the frame identity and the endpoint condition give Phi_{I_m}, the shear H<-H+D, on every original row'. It never states the identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m, nor how it holds (P_{U_a^perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m on X_a, zero source and identity sink elsewhere, 1169-1171). The -P_{U_a} sources appear only as rank exceptions. The verdict is the conservative one, since the condition is named but not given.
The plan has the factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2, a shear of rank a costing exactly a interchanges plus O(V), and the node's recursive calls summing to exactly s (S1.1.6.5, quoting 1543).

The plan has children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and tau=1-2^-50 from eta_b>20*2^-50 and m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-20*2^-50)>m(1-eta), hence s/W<m^tau and F_k=O(e^tau). The bound log m<20 behind the middle inequality (1332) is used without being stated.

central.summary: The plan rebuilds most of the chain behind the central saving: frames, labels, rank equals dimension change with the N rank-one source exceptions, the budget s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b, the strict saving from L/N=100/539, edges as recursive calls, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^-50. The weak link is the endpoint identity M_sink-M_source=I_m, which the plan names but never states or justifies. The concrete parameters h=100, N and m are also never given.
